newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker as budget impact fades.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker as budget impact fades.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended weaker around C$1.3594 (US$0.7356) on Wednesday from Tuesday's close of C$1.3545 (US$0.7382) as the impact of Canada's budget faded * Stop-loss selling briefly pushed Canada unit to C$1.3600 (US$0.7352) around midday, but firmed after domestic buyers stepped in, traders said * Canada's Martin would accept finance portfolio again
Canadian dollar ended weaker on Wednesday as the impact of a stay-the-course federal budget on Tuesday faded from investors' minds.
The Canadian dollar finished around C$1.3594 (US$0.7356) from Tuesday's close at C$1.3545 (US$0.7382). The currency is expected to trade between C$1.3590 and C$1.3615 overnight.

"I was a little surprised Canada didn't get stronger on the back of the budget, but when it didn't some of the long Canada positions started to unwind," one trader said. Much of the positive budget news such as a lower-than-projected 1996/97 deficit was already priced into the market.
Traders said there was little reaction to Finance Minister Paul Martin's comment on Wednesday that he would agree to return to the finance portfolio if the government wins the next election.

Martin also said he favors setting debt-to-gross domestic product targets for the country. Martin did not specify what the target should be, but he said a target of 60 percent was not ambitious enough.
On the crosses, Canada's dollar rose to 1.2486 marks from Tuesday's close of 1.2442 marks and rose to 91.55 yen from 91.45 yen.
